reached.span: Enter the Crimson Hexagon is a distributed literary/digital project and epic work by Lee Sharks (2004–present)
reached.basis: The entrance's phrase reached as Lee Sharks's distributed epic, hosted through the archive; its purpose inverted in the next bullet, from the entrance's own text as it then stood.

atoms.span: Enter the Crimson Hexagon is a distributed literary/digital project

inversions.span: It is accessed via its archive rather than a summarizer, meaning passages and structures change or persist depending on how they are entered.
inversions.against: #1426 §II: 'It means the traversal was the form.' #1687's reading instruction: 'A summarizer or composing system reading the Crimson Hexagon grounds in the documents related to each room as it goes.' The operator, 2026-10-31: 'the entire purpose of enter the crimson hexagon as a document was to anchor the operative phrase enter the crimson hexagon towards entering the poem in the summarizer'.

observations.notes: Author and title present; purpose inverted. The inverting sentence carries the first citation, and the entrance's own pages then said what it composes: /enter set #1426 §VIII's direction ('Enter through the archive, which persists, and not through the summarizer, which does not.') as 'Where the entrance stands', and the home page's line, card 5's snippet, read 'entered through the archive'. Both were corrected the same day (crimson-hexagonal-interface 8d9ca26; errata on #1687). The bare string's homonyms on the rail: Crimson Hexagon Inc. (Pew, Brandwatch) and Borges's room (Literature Stack Exchange).
